From the moment I was admitted, I noticed a clear difference in the way staff interacted with patients and their families. The doctors were extremely polite, attentive, and made sure to check every small detail regarding my health. The nursing staff was equally impressive—always smiling, professional, and caring throughout my stay. What truly stood out was how frequently they checked on me after surgery—every 30 minutes, someone was there to ask how I was doing, which made me feel very well cared for.

Another highlight was the hygiene. The hospital floors were spotless, and there was absolutely no unpleasant medicinal smell—something that’s often hard to avoid in hospitals. The housekeeping staff (especially the aunties) were doing an excellent job maintaining cleanliness at all times.

The only reason I’m not giving a perfect experience is the billing process—it took a bit longer than expected. But apart from that, I had a very smooth, satisfying experience and felt that the care I received was truly worth it.

Highly recommended!

featured_reviews.name: Diago Fernandes
featured_reviews.review_text:
Extremely Disappointing Experience.

My experience at Ramakrishna Mission Hospital was deeply unsatisfactory and alarming. For an institution associated with such a respected name, the overall standards of care, hygiene, and management are far below acceptable levels.

The trainee doctors displayed an arrogant, careless, and dismissive attitude, lacking basic empathy and professionalism. Patient concerns were often brushed aside, creating unnecessary stress and frustration.

Cleanliness is a major issue throughout the hospital. Washrooms and patient areas were unhygienic, poorly maintained, and visibly dirty, raising serious concerns about infection control and patient safety.

Despite booking and paying for a “First Class” room, the condition was horrible and unacceptable—dirty floors, stained and broken tiles, poorly maintained toilets, foul smell, and an overall neglected environment. This was misleading and completely unworthy of a first-class facility.

Time management is extremely poor. Long waiting hours, lack of communication, and no respect for patients’ time indicate weak administration and poor coordination.

The only positive aspect of this hospital experience was the professionalism and dedication of Dr. Ulhas Nadkarni and Dr. Amarish Warty. Both doctors were knowledgeable, patient, and compassionate, and they treated us with respect and genuine care. Their conduct reflects what medical professionalism should look like.

Unfortunately, apart from these two doctors, the hospital suffers from poor hygiene, unprofessional trainee behavior, misleading facilities, and inefficient management. Immediate corrective action is required.

I would not recommend this hospital unless serious improvements are made.

Update: I’ve experienced both private consultation and general OPD at Holy Spirit Hospital, and overall, it has been a bad experience.

The campus itself is beautiful and well maintained. Online appointment booking is smooth, while offline booking starts at 7:30 am and doctors typically begin consultations from around 8:30 am.

The private consultation experience (ENT, in my case) was genuinely good. The doctor gave adequate time, listened patiently, and the interaction felt reassuring and professional. However, this comes at a cost, as the visit including diagnostics ended up in the range of ₹3,000–4,000.

The general OPD experience was very bad. The charges are in the range of ₹400-700.

Earlier I had positive experiences with  Gastroenterology and Surgery. I was very much impressed with the surgeon, but his opinion was outrightly dismissed by 3 other senior surgeons and physicians. I realised he kept focussing on a know problem which wasn't connected to my pain.  Gastroenterologist doesn't do any physical examination to understand the location of pain or confirm hemorrhoids. Seems, he only checks you during pricey colonoscopy and endoscopy procedures.

My experience with General Medicine and Urology OPD was disappointing. In these departments, the main doctor and an assistant doctor sit at the same small table and consult two different patients simultaneously.

featured_reviews.review_text:
It’s deeply disappointing to see a hospital, regarded by many as esteemed, refuse emergency care based on discriminatory policies.

They turned away an accident victim who could have been saved had they fulfilled their duty and provided treatment, instead of shooing them away.

Such actions are not only unethical but also a blatant violation of basic human rights and medical responsibilities.

featured_reviews.name: Sanaya Eranee
featured_reviews.review_text: On 18th June 2021 I went to Parsi General Hospital for my 1st dose Covishield vaccine. I was truly impressed with the way the entire process was undertaken - seamless and so well managed. I reached the Hospital at 8.30am and by exactly 8.58am I was vaccinated and seated in the wait area with a hot cup of tea given by the kind and hardworking staff. I wish to commend not only all the frontline workers, and the Team involved in this vaccination drive, but those nameless, silent faces of the Security, pantry boy and help staff all of whom went out of their way to help each and every person with courtesy, a big smile and the most polite demeanor. A Salute and Kudos to you all. I thank you very much and hope many people get to experience the wonder that is Parsi General Hospital.
